text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

g.font-family: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

text.tspan: KEYS
select a project
open it and see its sessions, esc comes back
move its allocation by 5 points
u
unset this target: back to an even split with the rest
e
unset every target at once
p
priority: high → normal → low, who gets spare capacity first
space
move it up: hidden to RECENT, RECENT to ACTIVE
x
move it down: ACTIVE to RECENT, RECENT to hidden
f
pin the row to the top of the list
d
mark it done: hands its unspent share to the others now
b n
mark it blocked, or needs-more
m
show every project, not just the first screenful
s
settings: columns, theme, status line, what to protect
r
read everything again now
? q
this help · quit
READING A ROW
A star means you pinned it, and pinned rows keep the order you pinned them in. A number after it is how many Claude
Code windows are open in that project, shown only when there is more than one. A dimmed row is holding its share
while nothing runs there.
THE TWO TABLES
ACTIVE is what shares your window. A project joins it on its own the moment you open Claude Code there, and stays
after you close it, holding whatever target you gave it.
RECENT is everything else SaveMyTokens has seen, holding nothing. Space moves the selected project up a level and x
moves it down, so x on a RECENT row hides it for good. Press m to see what is hidden and space to bring one back. A
target you set is remembered wherever the project sits.
A filled dot means a session is open there right now. Only those spend the window, so one sitting in ACTIVE with
nothing running lends its share to the rest and takes it back when you return.
ALLOCATION AND PRIORITY
Allocation is what you asked for: the share of the window this project should get. Move it with the arrows.
Priority decides who gets the leftovers. Capacity is released whenever a project finishes or sits idle under its
target, and that spare goes to every HIGH project first, then NORMAL, then LOW. It is an order, not a weighting: a
LOW project gets nothing while a HIGH one still has room.
So allocation is your intent and priority is the tie-break. If pinned targets already add up to the whole window
there is no spare, and priority does nothing.
THE STATUS LINE
Installed. It is the only place your 5h and 7d usage is published, and it is what proves a session is still open, so
without it nothing here is live. Change its shape with P.
THE NUMBERS
5h and 7d are published figures, not ours. Share is measured from the tokens in your transcripts. Used of it is
their number split by that share, so the split between rows is ours, not theirs.
WHEN IT GETS TIGHT
Claude is told to wind down at 50/80/90% of a project's target. Change it with P.
ANYTHING ELSE
Questions, bugs and ideas: hello@offbeatport.com
